directive.thread_id: film repository port 2026-11-05, lane film-tools: the narrator tools of a film
directive.quote: Finish the port of the film repository so it can be retired: move each job to its correct home, porting the correct parts one to one and never rebuilding from scratch what already worked; move the code byte for byte, then make what it fixed arguments and settings.

targets.baseline_commit_message: check-every-claim-against-its-facts-and-sources: a film's fact gate, source extracts and world reader, moved byte for byte

preserve: every claim rule of the gate: coverage of script and screen texts, support said by someone other than the narrator, topic accounting with considered reasons, transcript and source quotes, strength scales bound to a support, numbers derived from cited numbers within their qualifier, bounds against world facts, comparisons, quantity containers, frames with observed and shown, private, believed, past, planned and conflicting facts, claims recorded as statements, hedge and attribution words
the world's own check runs first and stops every shot when it fails
report lines FAIL / ok and the last line '<label> <id>: PASS | n failures'
allowed_deltas: the folders it read from where it sat (shots, claims, scripts, sources, frames, world) are request fields

rules.json is the person's list:settings row, read with tools/settings request_settings; its subject-words key is subject_words; the subject's and narrator's names and the hedge row label are settings words
the hedge phrases come in the request (the person's no-hedge check row) instead of a file
path_map for paths written on another computer; a missing file is a failed shot, not a crash
do-work/check_claims.py is the command (one JSON request, one JSON answer) in place of main()
banned_substitutions: a second claim checker beside this one
rules or names written into the code
_paths: The source lives in a private repository, so it is named by the BLAKE3 identity of its path (path_multihash); a checkout of that repository beside this one finds it. Lines holding a person's name or a private path are left out of the sources (each source names its lines), so they never reach this public repository; the first source is the byte copy.
